# Hand-off test vectors

Fixtures for the [hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md): requests that a certifier must accept or refuse, and answers that a requester must install or refuse, with the expected outcome and reason code of each in `v1/manifest.json`.

Everything under `v1/` is public material made with throw-away software keys by `generate.py`. No private key is kept. The script is the record of how the files were made; running it again makes different bytes, so the committed files are the fixtures. A change to a vector that flips its outcome is a new contract version (a new directory).

Every key, serial and signature comes from a stream over one seed, with one stream for each part of the set, and ECDSA signs deterministically (RFC 6979). A run with the same seed in `RITUEEL_VECTOR_SEED` makes the same bytes, and a part added to the script changes no file of the other parts; without it the seed is random. The seed is not kept in the repository, because keys derived from a published seed would be private key material in it ([public content](../../docs/contributing/public-content.md)).

The same run writes the [root list vectors](../root-list/README.md), the [SSH CA key list vectors](../ssh-ca-keys/README.md) and the [CRL vectors](../crl/README.md), because the lists and the CRLs are signed by the same test roots. To regenerate all four, run `python3 testdata/hand-off/generate.py testdata/hand-off/v1 testdata/root-list/v1 testdata/ssh-ca-keys/v1 testdata/crl/v1` (Python 3 with `cryptography`) after removing the old files of the sets, then `just check-vectors`: it fails when the manifest and the tracked files disagree. A request of type `ssh-ca-key` has an SSH signature that `ssh-keygen -Y check-novalidate -n ssh-ca-key@ritueel.id -s <stem>.sshca.sig < <stem>.sshca.pub` checks. `.gitignore` keeps key files out of the repository and lets the `.pem` and `.asc` files under `testdata/` in; every key here is a throw-away test key whose private half was never written.

## Extended key usage

A request for an intermediate must state its extended key usage, not critical, and the certificate carries it exactly as requested: the same purposes in the same order, with the same flag. Every X.509 request in the set states `serverAuth` (the default of `make_csr` in `generate.py`), except the cases named `x509-eku-*`:

- accepted, and answered with an installed certificate that carries the same extension: `x509-eku-server-and-client` (`serverAuth` and `clientAuth`, in that order) and `x509-eku-client-only` (`clientAuth`);
- refused with `policy`, each differing from `x509-software-valid` in its extended key usage alone: `x509-eku-missing` (none stated), `x509-eku-any` (`anyExtendedKeyUsage`), `x509-eku-code-signing` (`codeSigning`), `x509-eku-server-and-code-signing` and `x509-eku-server-and-any` (an allowed purpose beside one that is not), `x509-eku-critical` (the extension marked critical) and `x509-eku-purpose-twice` (`serverAuth` named twice).

The answers to `x509-response-request`, which states `serverAuth`, have these faults, each refused with `profile` and valid in everything else: `x509-response-eku-dropped` (the extension is left out), `x509-response-eku-other` (`clientAuth` instead), `x509-response-eku-widened` (`serverAuth` and `clientAuth`) and `x509-response-eku-critical` (the extension marked critical). `x509-response-eku-reordered` answers `x509-eku-server-and-client` with the same two purposes in the other order. On the floor, `x509-floor-eku-dropped` copies every requested extension except this one.

The flag is decided (2026-11-14; [the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request) and [record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 47): the extension is not critical, as for a subordinate CA in the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements (2.3.1, 7.1.2.5.1 and 7.1.2.6.1: `extKeyUsage`, critical "N"). `generate.py` still holds it in one constant, `EKU_CRITICAL`, which is `False`; every request and every certificate takes its value from it, except the cases that set the flag on purpose.

## Name constraints, the subject and the form of a request

These cases are made with a software key under the development configuration, each differing from `x509-software-valid` in one thing, and each group is drawn from a stream of its own, so that no other file changes. A refused case gives `policy` unless it says otherwise. Every older accepted request already follows these rules (lower-case names, an ASCII subject of printable characters, name constraints present, one extension request, PKCS #10 version 0, `ecdsa-with-SHA384`), so none was changed for them. The expected code of each case that the Go request reader of `internal/pki` can judge from the bytes was checked against that reader on 2026-11-14 (run again on its built form for the cases of round 4: a request is read with `ParseRequestFile`, and with `IntermediateTBS` for the keys and names of the roots). The cases that need the policy lists, the proofs or the stores are judged by the certifier and not by that reader.

The reference policy of the manifest lists, besides the URI host `example.org`, the URI host `.example.org` (a period and a domain) and the DNS name `example.org` (`permitted_dns_names`), so that the accepted cases below are inside it.

**A third configuration.** A badly formed name is also outside the policy, because the policy lists whole names. So that the form rule is tested alone, the manifest has a third configuration, `development-listed-names`: the development policy, with the badly formed names of the cases listed in `permitted_uri_hosts` and `permitted_dns_names`. Each refused case of a name form has a twin with the suffix `-listed`: the same files against that configuration, where the name is inside the policy and only its form can refuse it, with the same code. A certifier that has the rule of equality with a listed name and no rule for the form passes the first and fails the second. `x509-nc-dns-label-63` and `x509-nc-dns-name-253` are accepted under it (the longest label and the longest name, listed there).

- **Name constraints** ([the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request)). Each case permits the URI host `example.org` and one more subtree. Accepted: `x509-nc-dns-valid` (the DNS name `example.org`), `x509-nc-uri-period-domain` (the URI constraint `.example.org`), `x509-nc-dns-label-63` and `x509-nc-dns-name-253` (a label of 63 characters; a name of 253). Refused, each with its `-listed` twin where the name is a form: `x509-nc-dns-empty`, `x509-nc-dns-upper-case` (`EXAMPLE.ORG`), `x509-nc-dns-wildcard` (`*.example.org`, written by hand, because the library refuses to), `x509-nc-dns-trailing-period`, `x509-nc-dns-leading-period`, `x509-nc-dns-numeric-last-label` (`example.123`), `x509-nc-dns-label-over-63` (64 characters), `x509-nc-dns-name-over-253` (254), `x509-nc-dns-hyphen-at-label-start`, `x509-nc-dns-hyphen-at-label-end`, `x509-nc-dns-empty-label` (`a..example.org`), `x509-nc-dns-underscore`, `x509-nc-uri-scheme` (`https://example.org`), `x509-nc-uri-port` (`example.org:8080`) and `x509-nc-uri-path` (`example.org/ca`). Refused for the kind of name, which no policy lists: `x509-nc-email`, `x509-nc-ip-range` (`10.0.0.0/8` permitted), `x509-nc-directory-name`, `x509-nc-other-name`, `x509-nc-x400-address`, `x509-nc-edi-party-name` and `x509-nc-registered-id`. Refused for the subtree: `x509-nc-subtree-minimum` (a minimum of 1), `x509-nc-subtree-minimum-0` (a minimum of 0 stated) and `x509-nc-subtree-maximum` (a maximum of 5), on the DNS name `example.org`. `x509-name-constraint-outside` and `x509-no-name-constraints` are older.
- **String types of the subject** ([the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request)). The subject is `O=acme` and the common name, with the attribute of the case added. Accepted: `x509-subject-dc-ia5-string` (domain components `org` and `example`, one in each relative name, as IA5String), `x509-subject-country-printable-string` (`C=NL`), `x509-subject-email-address-ia5-string`, `x509-subject-other-attribute-type` (an attribute type that the profile does not name, 1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1) and `x509-subject-multi-valued-relative-name` (`O` and `OU` in one relative name, in DER order). Refused: `x509-subject-dc-printable-string`, `x509-subject-bmp-string` (the common name), `x509-subject-country-utf8-string`, `x509-subject-country-three-characters`, `x509-subject-serial-number-utf8-string`, `x509-subject-dn-qualifier-utf8-string`, `x509-subject-email-address-utf8-string`, `x509-subject-common-name-ia5-string`, `x509-subject-printable-string-underscore` and `x509-subject-printable-string-at-sign` (a PrintableString outside its alphabet) and `x509-subject-value-not-a-string` (the common name is an INTEGER; OpenSSL 3.5.5 cannot read this file at all).
- **Characters, sizes and repeats in the subject** ([the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request)). Accepted: `x509-subject-common-name-64-characters` (the upper bound of RFC 5280, Appendix A.1), `x509-subject-organizational-unit-twice` (two relative names) and `x509-subject-domain-component-three-times` (`DC=corp`, `DC=example`, `DC=org`, each in a relative name of its own: an organisational unit and a domain component may stand any number of times, each in a relative name of its own). Refused: `x509-subject-common-name-65-characters` and `x509-subject-organization-65-characters` (the bound of a second attribute type), `x509-subject-empty-value` (a common name of no character), `x509-subject-non-ascii` (one `a` with a diaeresis), `x509-subject-two-spaces`, `x509-subject-trailing-space`, `x509-subject-common-name-twice` (two relative names) and `x509-subject-organizational-unit-twice-in-one-relative-name`.
- **The structure of the subject** ([the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request)). Refused with `malformed`: `x509-subject-empty` (no relative name), `x509-subject-empty-relative-name` (a set with no attribute), `x509-subject-content-fault-before-form-fault` (a PrintableString with `@` in the first relative name and attributes out of DER order in the second: the fault of form is told), `x509-subject-value-constructed` (the value is a constructed string), `x509-subject-value-followed-by-an-element` (an element after the value) and `x509-subject-unsorted-relative-name` (the two attributes of a relative name are not in DER order).
- **The keys and names of the roots** ([the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request)). Refused: `x509-request-root-key` and `x509-request-root-b-key` (a request for the key of root A, or of root B, signed by it) and `x509-subject-root-name` and `x509-subject-root-b-name` (the name of root A, or of B, written in capitals). The two roots are the two keys of the bundle; a reader that checks only the issuing root passes the second pair.
- **The form of the request** ([the hand-off contract](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-request)). Refused with `malformed`: `x509-request-extension-request-twice` (two extension-request attributes that differ: the basic constraints, key usage and name constraints in one, the extended key usage in the other; a verifier that merges them sees all four, and `openssl req -text` shows one), `x509-request-extension-request-two-values` (one attribute with two values), `x509-request-extension-request-empty` (an extension request with no extension), `x509-request-signature-algorithm-not-well-formed` (the signature algorithm element is an octet string), `x509-request-challenge-password` (a challenge password beside the extension request; the value is made up), `x509-request-version-number-1` and `x509-request-version-number-2` (a request whose version number is 1, or 2; the contract requires 0), `x509-request-two-pem-blocks` and `x509-request-text-after-the-pem-block` (the file is one block and nothing else). The signatures of the form cases verify; OpenSSL 3.5.5 nevertheless warns "error while verifying CSR self-signature" for a version number other than 0, because it refuses one. Refused with `policy`: `x509-request-extension-twice` (the extended key usage stands twice in the one list) and `x509-request-extended-key-usage-empty` (an empty list of purposes). Refused with `possession-invalid`: `x509-request-sha256`, a request signed by a P-384 key with `ecdsa-with-SHA256`.

**Rules that have no vector yet**, and why:

- A request or a request file over 256 KiB: a file that large does not belong in the tree.
- Two faults in one request across the checks (a P-256 key beside a subject that is refused, a SHA-256 signature beside one): only the order inside a subject has a case (`x509-subject-content-fault-before-form-fault`); the others are not written yet.
- The other upper bounds of a value (a title, a locality, a state or province, a pseudonym, a serial number, an e-mail address, a name of 32768 characters) and a value of the other string types that RFC 5280 names (a TeletexString, a NumericString): the common name and the organisation show the rule, and one case for each type of value would only repeat it.
- A subtree with an element other than a minimum or a maximum after its base: the three cases of a minimum or a maximum show the rule.
- A request signed with SHA-1 or SHA-512 (SHA-256 is the case), and a request whose key is not P-384 other than P-256 (an RSA key): the same code, the same rule.
- A URI constraint whose name, without the period at its start, has 253 characters: the page counts it so, no case states it.
- A PEM block with a label other than `CERTIFICATE REQUEST`, or with headers; an extension whose critical flag is written as FALSE; a key that is not in the canonical form: refusals of the Go request reader that no page states, so no case states a result.
- The comparison of names with a run of spaces as one space: no value may hold two spaces, so no case can show it.

## The floor with `openssl`

The floor answers (`"floor": true` in the manifest) are certificates from a CA that is not ritueel, for the request `x509-response-request` ([the floor](../../docs/reference/hand-off-contract.md#the-floor-pkcs10-in-x509-out)). A CA tool makes one with a throwaway test CA. With OpenSSL 3.5.5, run on 2026-11-13 in a scratch directory:

```sh
openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-384 -noenc -keyout ca.key -out ca.pem \
  -subj "/CN=Example Floor CA (TEST ONLY)" -days 3650 -sha384 \
  -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE" -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign"
openssl x509 -req -in testdata/hand-off/v1/requests/x509-response-request.csr.pem -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key \
  -copy_extensions copyall -not_before 20261115120000Z -not_after 20271215120000Z -sha384 -out floor.cert.pem
```

The result passes the floor checks of the requester: `openssl verify -attime 1794744000 -CAfile ca.pem floor.cert.pem` prints `OK` at the vectors' clock; `openssl x509 -in floor.cert.pem -noout -pubkey` and `openssl req -in <the CSR> -noout -pubkey` print the same key; and `openssl x509 -in floor.cert.pem -noout -ext basicConstraints,keyUsage,nameConstraints,extendedKeyUsage` shows the four requested extensions, as the CSR asked: the first three critical, and `extendedKeyUsage` (`serverAuth`) critical or not as `EKU_CRITICAL` says (not critical now). `-copy_extensions copyall` is what makes it a floor certificate: without it OpenSSL drops every requested extension (it prints `No extensions in certificate`), the extended key usage among them, and the requester refuses the result for its profile, as it refuses the vectors `x509-floor-extensions-dropped` and `x509-floor-eku-dropped`. Delete `ca.key` when you are done.
